svg.title: A nurse faces an ethical conflict on her unit and is unsure how to proceed. Which actions are appropriate steps in ethical decision making? Select all that apply.
svg.desc: Good ethical reasoning is slow and shared: get the facts, check your own bias, name the conflict, weigh options, and use the ethics committee. Deciding fast and alone is the trap. It feels decisive but skips the reasoning that justifies the choice.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Ethical Principles
Read the situation
A nurse faces an ethical conflict on her
unit and is unsure how to proceed. Which
actions are appropriate steps in ethical
decision making? Select all that apply.
What fits here
Gather the clinical facts before judging
the situation · Identify how her own
values are shaping her reaction · Name the
competing principles and list possible
courses of action · Bring…
Why it fits
Good ethical reasoning is slow and shared:
get the facts, check your own bias, name
the conflict, weigh options, and use the
ethics committee. Deciding fast and alone
is the trap. It feels decisive but skips
the reasoning that justifies the choice.
